from.place: The torsion part: 'The torsion subsheaf T is the kernel of F to j_*F_eta ... hence quasi-coherent' and 'the torsion-free quotient E := F/T'

title: Torsion subsheaf and torsion-free quotient
statement: Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with generic point $\eta$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. The local sections whose image in $\mathcal F_\eta$ is zero form a quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{tors}}\subseteq\mathcal F$. At each $x\in X$ its stalk is the torsion submodule of $\mathcal F_x$ over the domain $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and the quotient $\mathcal F/\mathcal F_{\mathrm{tors}}$ is torsion-free. Equivalently, $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{tors}}$ is the kernel of the natural map $\mathcal F\to j_*\mathcal F_\eta$, where $j:\operatorname{Spec}k(X)\to X$ is the generic-point morphism and $k(X)$ is its function field [def-sc-function-field].
